note: Adapted from the species-level description in Hill (1942), original in English; the original work has it as Eutermes dalbiensis sp. nov. (the OCR gives the heading as 'Eutermee'), the type locality Dalby (Qld), described from a series of soldiers and workers taken in shallow galleries under a stone. The original gives the alate as 'Not known', so that section is not included. The head length of the soldier is given in the original as a single value, 1.45 mm (not a range), and is transcribed as such. OCR misreadings: 'bastille' = 'hastilis', 'hent upwards' = 'bent upwards', 'sth' = '5th', 'Man-dibles' broken across lines = mandibles, 'hastills' = 'hastilis'.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A rather small species with a dark orange head and antennae of 13 or 14 long segments. Very close to E. hastilis, differing as follows: body larger, head a little darker in tone and more constricted, more concave at the middle in dorsal view, nasus much longer and stouter and upturned. The alate is not recorded in the original.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: A rather small species with a dark orange head and antennae of 13 or 14 long segments. Very close to E. hastilis, differing as follows: body larger, head a little darker in tone and more constricted, more concave at the middle in dorsal view, nasus much longer and stouter and upturned. Antennae usually 14-segmented; the basal segments variable; usually segment 1 long, nearly cylindrical; segment 2 slightly shorter than segment 4, nearly cylindrical; segment 3 shorter than segments 2 and 4; segment 5 slightly shorter than segment 4; segments 6—13 long and narrow, segment 14 shorter than segment 13. Segments 3 and 4 of one or both antennae are often more or less closely fused, or merge into a single segment almost as long as segment 1 (the latter giving a 13-segmented antenna). Mandibles usually with a pointed tooth. Measurements: body length 4.25—4.60 mm; head length (to apex of nasus) 1.45 mm; head width 0.74—0.80 mm; pronotum width 0.55 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Like the worker of E. hastilis, but the antennae as in the soldier. Postclypeus slightly more than half as long as wide. Measurements: body length 5.00—5.50 mm; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.72—1.76 mm; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.95—1.00 mm; head width 1.28—1.32 mm; pronotum width 0.77—0.80 mm.
